title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 3
paragraphs: It had originally been proposed, even before they sent to Sicily to seek allies, that the fleet should be placed in the charge of the Athenians. When the allies opposed this, the Athenians yielded, as they had it deeply at heart that Greece should be saved, and they saw that if there were disagreement among themselves over the leadership, Greece would perish. In this they judged rightly, for discord among those of the same race is worse than unified war, by as much as war is worse than peace. Being convinced of this truth, they did not contend, but gave way for as long as they urgently needed the allies — as their later conduct proved. For when, having driven the Persian away from themselves, they were now fighting for his land and no longer for their own, they used the arrogance of Pausanias as a pretext and stripped the Lacedaemonians of the leadership. But that happened later.
